title: VaultWork
description: A work in a project's library (ADR 0052): prior work consulted for the project, used or set aside, with where to find it, how closely it was read and what the project took from it. Notes cite it (`cites`) with the role it plays; its citation is exported as BibTeX, CSL-JSON or an annotated bibliography.

work_id.title: VaultWorkId
work_id.description: A work's identifier in the project's library, also its citation key: kebab-case, the first author's family name, the year and a word of the title (`vaswani-2017-attention`), or the project and owner for code (`karpathy-nanogpt`). It does not change.

project_id.title: ProjectId
project_id.description: Stable project identifier (lowercase slug). Never a path; paths live in the local registry.

kind.title: VaultWorkKind
kind.description: What a work is. paper: published in a journal or conference (`venue`). preprint: arXiv and the like. book, thesis, report (a technical report). repo: a code repository. software: a released package. dataset, model: a published dataset or model card. docs: documentation. article: a blog post or essay. thread: an issue, pull request, forum or Q&A thread. talk: a talk or video.

authors.description: As `Family, Given` (or an organisation's name), in the work's order. `others` for et al.

venue.description: Journal, conference, publisher, institution or site (`NeurIPS 2017`, `GitHub`).

arxiv.description: The arXiv identifier, `1706.03762` (a version, `v2`, when it matters).

version.description: The commit, tag or release consulted (code, data, models, docs).

reading.title: VaultWorkReading
reading.description: How closely the work was read: unread (found, not read yet), abstract (the abstract or README only), skimmed, read (the parts that matter, closely). Said plainly so a reader knows how much a citation rests on.

summary.description: What the work says or does, in two to five sentences of your own words: its question, method and result as they bear on this project. Markdown with LaTeX. Never pasted from the work.

takeaway.description: What this project took from it, or why it was set aside, in one or two sentences.

found_for.description: The problem or question it was looked up for (a note's `[[id]]` may be named).

found_via.description: How it was found: the search and where it was run, or the work that cited it.

task_id.title: TaskId
task_id.description: AblationKit task identifier (UI- or agent-first task).

created_at.title: Timestamp
created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a `Z` suffix and optional fractional seconds.

updated_at.title: Timestamp
updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a `Z` suffix and optional fractional seconds.

created_by.title: ResearchActor
created_by.description: Who made a change: a human session, an agent token or the system. Work under a task links the task (`task:ID`).

updated_by.title: ResearchActor
updated_by.description: Who made a change: a human session, an agent token or the system. Work under a task links the task (`task:ID`).

archived_at.title: Timestamp
archived_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with a `Z` suffix and optional fractional seconds.
